answers.answer: Each player takes twelve ordinary turns: three ordinary rounds per season across four seasons. Courtship rounds (4, 8, 12, 16) have no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
answers.evidence: Overview: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns’; ‘Courtship is an event, with no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.’

answers.answer: Host in order: rotate service (Quarters to Available, then Expended to Quarters); resolve the round event; resolve applicable ongoing monument/Servants’ Hall effects; choose an activity; play exactly the required gentry; provide required service; take favours with all positive before all negative; optionally buy one tile; then send used servants to Expended, played gentry to personal discard, and return the activity tile to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. Only the last player in order advances the marker one space after cleanup.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Hosting an activity, steps 1–8.

answers.answer: Pass order: all servants directly to Available; all gentry in your discard to hand; resolve round event, then ongoing effects; choose either £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; last player advances the marker. Ongoing-effect servants used during the pass go to Expended at turn end. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.
answers.evidence: Passing: ‘all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh → optional one tile purchase’.

answers.answer: Yes. The end-of-step-2 screening reputation of 6.1 is used for the PR6 tile and guests throughout this activity; later Service Help losses do not invalidate it. Service Help costs 3 increments each and can move one servant per action only from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service, never from Expended. Four actions cost 12 increments, taking actual reputation to 3.4 as stated.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions: screening is fixed at end of step 2; later loss does not invalidate. Service Help moves one Quarters servant to Available for 3 increments.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; within those groups, choose the order. At minimum reputation (1.1), you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to avoid the loss: minimum-reputation protection means losses beyond minimum are ignored, while favours remain mandatory. A money penalty must be fully payable; use positive money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money. If still unable to pay, you cannot play that guest/tile.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6; Reputation, wealth and special actions: ‘A money penalty must be fully payable.’

answers.answer: Borrow Money: lose 2 reputation increments, gain £100, repeatable. Service Help: lose 3 increments, move one servant from Quarters to Available, repeatable. Refresh Market: lose 4 increments, fully refresh, once per turn for this special action. At minimum 1.1 you cannot take any special action. Service Help cannot take a servant straight from Expended.
answers.evidence: Special actions table and minimum-reputation rule.

answers.answer: Host Butler’s Room as a Servant Hiring activity using an available butler or underbutler, with no gentry. Take up to two non-underbutler servants from Servants for Hire into Expended Service; there is no hiring fee. After upgrade, instead recruit one common footman, valet, or lady’s maid from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service. Unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: Butler’s Room entry.

answers.answer: A housekeeper may substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With Brushing Room in your tableau, a footman may substitute for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman) even while that type remains available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: substitutions paragraph.

answers.answer: The only way to acquire an underbutler is to buy Butler’s Pantry; take it from supply into Expended Service. It is not immediately available: normal rotation moves it to Quarters at the next rotation and Available at the second subsequent rotation. Passing or Refresh Service VP card may make it available earlier; once it is in Quarters, Service Help or Servants’ Quarters can permit earlier use. An opponent cannot recruit it because it is unique, not common.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: Butler’s Pantry paragraph.

answers.answer: Market price is the space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier; Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. Price cannot be below £100. You cannot acquire a duplicate tile already owned. Reputation does not restrict purchasing, so an above-reputation tile may be bought.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: price and duplicate rules.

answers.answer: When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into rightmost spaces. Stack a drawn duplicate on its matching Market tile and draw again; if filling multiple spaces, sort only the new tiles by ascending sorting number. Reserve-eligible draws go straight to Reserve and are replaced by another draw. Buying one tile from a duplicate stack leaves the space occupied, so no refill occurs.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: ‘Refill’ paragraph.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later Service draws also go to Reserve, with that exception. After courtship 2, move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve; later PR1 draws go there too. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. Full Market refresh after each of the first three courtships is standard; refresh follows Reserve movement.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: ‘Open Reserve’ and ‘Refresh’; Overview confirms standard full seasonal refresh.

answers.answer: At ordinary courtships 1–3, return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall; score tile VP in the current theme’s face-up category, including negative tile VP. Highest wins one VP card and chooses one Fairchild for hand. If tied for highest, each tied player draws a VP card and no Fairchild is awarded. Everyone discards one objective; shuffle simultaneous discards together and put them face down at the deck bottom. Then open Reserve, refresh Market, reveal next theme, pass first-player marker anticlockwise, and advance the round marker.
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep, ordinary courtships and seasonal order.

answers.answer: Final courtship scores tile VP in all four revealed themes; a repeated category counts each time, including negative VP. Highest gets a VP card and Fairchild. Ties break by highest reputation level, ignoring wheel position; if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards under the tie rule. Discard the final objective, then players may use special actions and VP cards for benefits before moving to Wedding Bells and scoring. Only the Fairchild won in final courtship is retained for its 8 VP.
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep: Final courtship (round 16).

answers.answer: End-game sources: face-up improvement tile VP (including negatives); gentry in hand and discard (including negatives, family and final Fairchild); fulfilled objectives; reputation levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP; 2 VP per servant of any type/location; 1 VP per £200, rounded down; and retained VP-card printed VP. Tiebreaks: final Fairchild, then highest reputation level, then shared victory. The summary does not give a separate wealth-rounding procedure beyond 1 VP per £200 rounded down.
answers.evidence: Final VP table and tie paragraph.

answers.answer: Normally receive five objectives at setup and two at round 6; discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score. Additional objectives from Main Library or a VP card increase retained final objectives and do not cause an extra discard. Simultaneous discards are shuffled together and placed face down on the deck bottom. Tile objectives require owning the tile at game end, not upgrading it.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: objective retention paragraph.

answers.answer: A VP card can be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your own later turn (multiple cards allowed), and once after final courtship before scoring. Reveal and discard it to use its benefit; used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained unused cards stay hidden with objectives and score their printed VP; you cannot take both benefit and VP.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: VP-card paragraph.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after first use; an already-upgraded normal tile stays upgraded on later uses. Hybrids flip after every use and move to the newly face-up category. A tile that upgrades into an ongoing monument hosts only once, then becomes a monument and cannot host again; monument benefit starts on subsequent turns. Only a hybrid’s face-up category counts for courtship and objectives.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: normal tiles, hybrids, monuments.

answers.answer: Monuments give one reputation during the ongoing-effects step on ordinary hosting and passing turns, but not courtship; newly purchased monuments begin on a later turn. Servants’ Hall works in that same step on hosting or passing: place one available servant on it, reduce one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one yourself; that servant goes to Expended Service at turn end and cannot serve the activity. Do not target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: monuments and Servants’ Hall.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite: footman on tile, one casual guest from hand with normal guest service; double all guest favours, including negative; upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite: housekeeper on tile, one prestige guest from hand with normal guest service; double one chosen favour and resolve other favours normally; upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite: butler on tile, draw one prestige guest to attend with no personal guest service; double nonnegative favours, exclude negative favours from doubling; keep guest in discard at cleanup; upgrades into a monument. Each suite has a fixed one-guest count that cannot be changed.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: Suite activity table and fixed-count note.

answers.answer: Choose a random first player and give them the first-player marker. Starting to that player’s left and going clockwise, players choose available base family boards. Bonuses: Asquith adds the Dowager Countess as a fifth family card; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gains £300; York adds a footman to Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 5.

answers.answer: Stack reputation counters 1/2, 3/4, 5/6 and Max with 1 showing and Max at bottom; do not use 7/8 counters. Start at 1.1 except Cavendish at 1.4. Each player gets one butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid and footman in Available Service; Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour and Bowling Green with starter icon showing; and Lord, Lady, Heir and Young Lady. Ponsonby alone starts with money (£300); other families start with none.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2, 3, and 5.

answers.answer: For three players, Servants for Hire receives three valets, three lady’s maids, six footmen, and two underbutlers total. No butlers or housekeepers are stocked. Unused servants are returned to the box and unavailable this game.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6: one valet and lady’s maid per player, two footmen per player, two underbutlers total; no butlers or housekeepers.

answers.answer: Separate starter guests from casual deck, shuffle them, and deal two to each player’s hand; shuffle every undealt starter back into the casual deck. Starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and follow normal casual rules, not a separate guest type during play.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4; Gentry, screening, dismissal and family.

answers.answer: For four players, select five double-sided monuments (one per player plus one). Choose at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments always go in the bag and do not count against that setup selection.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: Draw until six different eligible tiles fill the Market: PR3 or lower (including no PR), excluding Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments. Set ineligible tiles aside and return them to the bag after filling; stack eligible duplicates in the same space. Normal tiles show upgrade icon hidden; hybrids show underlined hybrid icon. Sort spaces by ascending printed sorting number beginning at the £300 space. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall, and double-sided monuments are ineligible.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8.

answers.answer: Put Alderley Hall standard side up with marker at round 1 and one reminder token per player above the track; shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal the first theme and keep revealed themes in order; put base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild face up on Alderley Hall. Thus the first theme is open, not hidden, and old revealed themes remain in play.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9; Overview describes open courtship.

answers.answer: At hosting rotation, a servant in Quarters moves to Available first; a servant in Expended moves to Quarters. Each advances one space only. An unused servant already Available remains Available.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 1: move Quarters to Available first, then Expended to Quarters; unused Available servants remain available.

answers.answer: No. The event resolves before choosing/hosting an activity, so a Private Study that is not already upgraded at that step earns no Fair reward even if hosted and upgraded later that turn. An already-upgraded Study gives £300 and 2 reputation. Village Fair is on standard spaces 3 and 9.
answers.evidence: Round-track events: Village Fair spaces 3 and 9; reward only if Study is already upgraded at this step.

answers.answer: Resolve the round-track event before ongoing effects: during hosting after service rotation, or during passing after servants and discarded gentry return. On space 6 draw two objectives and keep both secret. Passing players receive the event too because all players’ turns resolve the event at that position.
answers.evidence: Round-track events paragraph/table; events apply on each player’s turn.

answers.answer: Yes. During National Holiday ignore PR on all tiles and guests when hosting, even for a low-reputation player. All other requirements still apply, including gentry counts/types and service.
answers.evidence: Round-track events: National Holiday on space 14.

answers.answer: Builders’ Holiday permits any number of Market and/or Reserve purchases within funds. Complete all purchases before sliding/refilling; tiles retain the space or Reserve price plus modifier from before the sequence. Do not refresh between purchases by special action or VP card. Market Purchase VP cards use the same single-unchanged-market rule, so no between-purchase refresh. The summary does not separately state whether original prices apply beyond this unchanged-price rule; that rule supports the same price during the sequence.
answers.evidence: Round-track events: Builders’ Holiday; Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card paragraph.

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside; leave Reserve unchanged. Refill all six spaces under normal refill rules, then return the set-aside Market tiles to the bag and mix them. Removed Market tiles cannot reappear in that same refresh; Reserve tiles are left unchanged.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: Refresh paragraph.

answers.answer: Reputation symbols are increments; moving past position 5 to 1 raises a level, and past 1 to 5 lowers a level. A level spans five increments. Standard range is 1.1 through 7.5 (Max.5); losses below 1.1 are ignored. At Max.5 excess reputation is lost unless spent immediately on special actions; special actions can be used before or during a reputation favour to make room.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions: increments, range and Max.5 rules.

answers.answer: Money is public, and players may not give or receive money between them in this mode. Never spend more money than held. The common supply is unlimited; use proxies if needed.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions: Money held is public; supply unlimited.

answers.answer: Two ladies may include female family members or female guests. Two casual guests must be casual guest cards and exclude family. You may not exceed or fall short of printed attendee counts. Family requires no personal service and has no PR threshold; family cards have no PR.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 4: exact numbers/types; ladies includes female family or guests; casual requirements exclude family. Reputation screening paragraph.

answers.answer: Ordinary guest-invite favour: draw one card from the indicated guest deck, reveal it to everyone, and add it to hand. Screening invite: draw the stated number, choose the stated number to keep, reveal only kept cards and add them to hand; put rejected cards on the bottom of the guest deck without revealing them.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family: Invite Guest favour and screening guests.

answers.answer: Dismissal is always optional, so you need not dismiss if you have no unwanted guest. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, current activity, or discard, including one just drawn earlier in Enjoy Favours. Family cannot be dismissed. Put the guest on the bottom of its matching deck; it is no longer yours, does not return on passing, and does not score for you.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family: dismissal paragraph.

answers.answer: Lord: £200. Lady: choose either screen two casual guests and keep one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Young Lady: draw one casual guest; also gain two reputation if a male prestige guest attends the same activity. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation. Lady and Heir offer choices; Dowager gives both benefits. Young Lady’s draw and conditional reputation bonus are both benefits.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family: base family card table and text.

answers.answer: She gains the two-reputation admirer bonus only if a male prestige guest attends. A male casual guest does not trigger it; a female prestige guest does not trigger it; Charles Fairchild does trigger it because he is a male prestige guest. The Young Lady still draws one casual guest in every case.
answers.evidence: Young Lady: draws one casual guest; bonus if a male prestige guest attends. Charles is explicitly male prestige.

answers.answer: Charles is a male prestige guest with no PR, requires a valet, and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a female prestige guest with no PR, requires a lady’s maid, and gives both one prestige guest and two reputation. They are guests, not family; neither has family dismissal immunity, and both may be dismissed normally.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family: Fairchild and favours paragraphs.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and makes you lose one reputation. Minimum-reputation protection applies, so a player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
answers.evidence: Gentry section: base gossip effects; reputation section: at minimum cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.

answers.answer: A Barn gives one reputation each time you host an Estate activity. Merely owning an Estate tile or passing gives no reputation.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: Barn paragraph.

answers.answer: Ordinary hosting rotation moves all Quarters servants to Available, then all Expended servants to Quarters, each one space. Servants’ Quarters improvement lets you use one servant still in Quarters after rotation directly, in addition to Available, without reputation cost; send it to Expended at turn end. Service Help instead costs 3 reputation increments to move one Quarters servant to Available and is repeatable; it cannot move directly from Expended.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: Servants’ Quarters tile and service mechanism table.

answers.answer: Private Study’s front activity requires a butler and two family, with no tile favour. After first use it upgrades permanently to an ongoing tile; it cannot be hosted repeatedly. The upgraded tile gives £300 and two reputation on Village Fair rounds without staffing or hosting it.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: Private Study paragraph.

answers.answer: Before upgrading, Main Library requires a butler and two family and draws one extra objective. After upgrading, it requires a butler and three family and draws one VP card. Extra objectives increase the number retained for final scoring and do not cause an extra discard.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: Main Library paragraph; Objectives and VP cards retention rule.

answers.answer: Objective VP card: draw two objectives, keep one, and put the other face down on the bottom of the objective deck. It gives one additional retained objective for final scoring.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: Objective benefit; it gives one additional retained objective.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants directly to Available, including those in Expended, and they can be used immediately. Service Help costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves only one servant from Quarters to Available; it cannot take from Expended.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: Refresh Service; special actions: Service Help.

answers.answer: Hire Servant VP card takes one servant from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutler, into Expended Service. It is not immediately available for service merely from being hired; the normal movement is needed. The summary identifies its destination but does not expressly state a separate immediate-use rule for this card.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: Hire Servant benefit says take one servant (not underbutler) into Expended Service.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Guest may return one gentry, including a family member, from your personal discard to hand. If done before Invite Gentry, you may then play that returned card as an attendee this turn if it meets requirements; returning it does not automatically play it.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: Refresh Guest benefit.

answers.answer: The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets, and lady’s maids; it excludes butler, housekeeper, and underbutler. Ordinary service VP gives 2 VP for every servant of all types and locations. The ten-servant objective gives 7 VP for at least ten servants total.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: basic-servant distinction; Final VP; objective table.

answers.answer: Yes. Upgraded Queen’s Suite is a monument and retains Estate category, so it counts for both monument and Estate category objectives. Upgraded Lionheart Suite is a monument and retains Prestige category, so it counts for both monument and Prestige category objectives. Hybrids count only in their currently face-up category.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: monument status/category and explicit Suite examples; hybrid rule.

answers.answer: Nature Group is 11 VP for Flower Room plus one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is 12 VP for Gabled Conservatory plus Main Library or North Library. Owning the required tiles at game end is sufficient; they need not have been used or upgraded.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: Nature and Domestic Group; group objectives note.

answers.answer: The prestige-guest objective gives 1 VP per prestige guest; the every-three-guests objective gives 1 VP per complete group of three nonfamily guests. A final Fairchild is a prestige guest and counts; incomplete groups of three do not score. Family is excluded from guest counts.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: ‘Guest excludes family; prestige guests include a final Fairchild’; Guest bonuses table.

answers.answer: The base reputation objective gives 7 VP for reaching maximum reputation level 7, regardless of wheel position. The wealth objective gives 10 VP for at least £1200. Ordinary reputation VP depends on level (levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28) and ignores wheel position; reputation tie resolution also uses level and ignores position.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference and Final VP table; courtship/game tiebreak paragraph.

answers.answer: Both West Terrace sides require one butler and exactly three family cards. Unupgraded favour: draw one prestige guest. Upgraded favours: draw one prestige guest and optionally dismiss one to four guests from hand, current activity, or discard to the bottom of the appropriate decks. It remains an activity tile on both sides and never becomes an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: West Terrace paragraph.

answers.answer: There is no maximum hand or personal discard size. Gentry in the discard pile still belong to you and score normally; passing returns them to hand unless dismissed.
answers.evidence: Gentry, screening, dismissal and family: opening paragraph.

answers.answer: You may inspect all Reserve tiles at any time and buy any one, including a tile under another in a stack; you are not limited to the top. Every Reserve tile is public.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: Open Reserve paragraph.

answers.answer: You may choose to host or pass. If the preferred activity lacks required gentry or service, choose another legal activity or pass; if no activity is possible, you must pass. Activity gentry counts and types must be exact.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Hosting steps 4–5.

answers.answer: Yes. On a passing turn you may take the free passing-benefit Market refresh, one paid special-action Refresh Market (4 reputation), and multiple Market Refresh VP-card benefits, each causing a separate full refresh. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the special-action refresh; pass and VP-card refreshes do not use it. Purchase-timing restrictions still apply, including no refresh between purchases in a Builders’ Holiday/Market Purchase sequence.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions: refresh availability; Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase restrictions.

answers.answer: No. Special actions are available at any time on your own turn, hosting or passing, with sufficient reputation; they are not interrupts during another player’s turn. On your turn they may be taken at any time, including before or during a reputation favour.
answers.evidence: Special actions paragraph: ‘at any time on your own turn, hosting or passing’; may act before or during reputation favour.

answers.answer: No. Printed favours are mandatory unless expressly optional, so an ordinary guest-invite favour cannot be declined while taking other favours. An optional dismissal is different: you may decline to dismiss, or choose an eligible guest to dismiss.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6: favours mandatory unless expressly optional; Gentry section: dismissal is always optional.
